title: Windows audit-policy clear command
description: Detects Auditpol commands requesting a system audit-policy clear or removal of all per-user audit policies. Verify the effective audit policy before concluding logging was impaired.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary with administrative access may clear Windows audit policy to prevent security-relevant activity from being recorded.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents that auditpol /clear disables system auditing for all subcategories, and MITRE explicitly identifies auditpol /clear and /remove /allusers as Windows logging impairment behavior.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify Auditpol commands that clear the system audit policy or remove every per-user audit policy while leaving policy queries, enablement and removal of one named user unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Treat a complete audit-policy reset as high impact and confirm an explicit operating-system or security-baseline change before accepting it.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete Auditpol command, account, elevation, parent process, device role and any remote-session context.
Check approved maintenance, image-build, recovery and security-baseline changes and compare the effective audit policy with the expected configuration.
Investigate subsequent logging gaps and related defense-impairment commands; restore policy and contain the endpoint when the reset is unauthorized.
false_positives: Approved audit-policy reset, operating-system recovery, image preparation or security-baseline maintenance

validation.expected_outcome: Match Auditpol system-policy clear and all-user removal commands; do not match policy inspection, normal enablement, another binary or removal of one user.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
